01 — About

A little about
me.

Hey, I'm Sresth Sarraf — a second-year BTech student at UPES Dehradun, studying Computer Science with a specialisation in Graphics & Gaming. Originally from Patna, Bihar, I've always been drawn to the intersection of technology and visual design.

I love the quiet precision of typography, the storytelling power of photography, the logic of code, the rhythm of guitar, and the emotion behind music. When I'm not in class, you'll find me designing in Canva or learning something new about type.

This site is both my personal space and my interactive typography notebook — a place where I learn, document, and share what I find.

07 — TypeLab

Interactive
Typography.

Hands-on modules to understand the language of type — from letterform anatomy to spacing and alignment.

hop

Click a concept →
Select any term on the left to highlight its line on the letterform and learn what it means in typography.

Kerning

TAVO

Kerning adjusts space between specific letter pairs for optical balance. T-A naturally needs tighter spacing than A-V.

Leading (Line Height)

The quick brown fox
jumps over the lazy
dog near the mill.

Named after lead strips in metal typesetting. Controls vertical space between lines of text.

Tracking

TYPEFACE

Tracking adjusts letter spacing uniformly across a whole word or block — unlike kerning which targets specific pairs.

X-Height

Xx

■ X-height — height of lowercase 'x', 'n', 'o'.
■ Baseline — the line all letters rest on.

Widows & Orphans

✗ Widow

Typography is the art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and appealing when well set.

A widow is a short word stranded alone at the end of a paragraph.

✗ Orphan

Typography is the art of arranging type to make written language readable and visually appealing.

An orphan is the first line of a paragraph isolated at the bottom of a column.

Flush Left / Ragged Right

Typography is the art of arranging type to make written language legible and appealing. The right edge varies naturally.

Most natural for Western reading. Best choice for body text in almost any context.

Flush Right / Ragged Left

Typography is the art of arranging type to make written language legible and appealing. The left edge is uneven.

Creates visual tension. Best used for captions, pull quotes, or sidebar content.

Centered

Typography is the art of arranging type to make written language legible and appealing. Both edges are ragged.

Elegant for headlines, invitations, and short display text. Hard for long passages.

Justified

Typography is the art of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and appealing when columns are properly set.

Both edges align to margins. Common in books. Can create "rivers" of space if poorly set.
